data.name: Dharitri
data.gender_notes: Dharitri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dharitri is the goddess of the earth, who is often depicted as the wife of Himalaya, the god of mountains. She is the protector of all beings and is believed to provide stability and nourishment to the world. The name Dharitri carries the meaning “Goddess of the Earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharitri usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine energy of nourishment, protection, and stability.
data.etymology: Dharitri belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharitri total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dharitri holds immense cultural significance in the Hindu tradition, symbolizing the vital role of Mother Earth in our lives. The goddess Dharitri is celebrated during various Hindu festivals and rituals, emphasizing the importance of revering nature and recognizing its essential relation to human life. Her image is deeply etched in Indian art, iconography, and literature, reflecting the profound sense of connection between the people and their land.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dharitri holds a profound spiritual significance for Hindus, representing the divine feminine energy, or Shakti, that nurtures and sustains all life on earth. Dharitri embodies the idea of stability, strength, and protection, offering comfort and sanctuary to all beings. She is revered as the source of everything that grows, the foundation that holds the universe together, and the eternal mother that watches over her children with unwavering love. Work Cited:
